item.title: New York Approves 22% Workers’ Compensation Cost Reduction
item.description: New York has approved a 21.9% reduction in workers compensation insurance premium rates, which the state says represents an estimated savings of more than $1 billion for businesses or an average of $1,779 per employer in the state. The loss cost rate reduction was approved by the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) and will take effect on October 1, 2026. The latest reduction in insurance costs is in addition to a reduced employer assessment rate to cover the costs of the New York State Compensation Insurance Rating Board.

item.title: SpeedBuilder Launches FormMaker 2.0
item.description: (Image credit: IIR/Gemini.) SpeedBuilder Systems (Columbia, S.C.) has released FormMaker 2.0, the latest version of its insurance document automation solution for property/casualty insurers. FormMaker is integrated with Microsoft Word and SpeedBuilder’s BindExpress Suite, according to a company statement. SpeedBuilder says FormMaker 2.0 is intended to address the complexity of maintaining insurance forms, including frequent product updates, changing regulations and state-specific filing requirements.

item.title: Global Commercial Insurance Rates Keep Falling; Down 8 Quarters in a Row
item.description: Global commercial insurance rates dropped by 6%, on average, in the second quarter of 2026, following a 5% decline in Q1 2026, according to Marsh’s latest Global Insurance Market Index (GIMI). (Editor’s note: Marsh’s Global Insurance Market Index skews toward larger account business). Property rates declined by 12% in Q2, while casualty rates increased 2%, driven largely by ongoing claims severity and litigation pressures in the US.

item.title: Berry Producer Driscoll’s Sued Over Alleged Use of Forever Chemicals
item.description: The world’s largest berry company will have to face a class-action lawsuit for supposed “greenwashing” after it allegedly failed to disclose the risk or use of pesticides containing what are known as “forever chemicals.” In a class-action lawsuit filed earlier this month in Superior Court in California against Driscoll’s Inc., plaintiffs claim violations of false advertising, unfair competition, and the state’s Consumer Legal Remedies Act. According to the plaintiffs, “Driscoll’s ran an environmentally friendly campaign—greenwashing its true farming and manufacturing practices that included these forever chemicals known to be extraordinarily difficult to clean up and break down and accumulate in the environment and living organisms, including humans.” According to the suit, testing found residue of a dozen different pesticides, eight considered PFAS, in the strawberries. Related: Mamavation Finds PFAS-Laden Pesticides in Driscoll’s Strawberries “Reasonable consumers are increasingly concerned about the environmental consequences of agricultural production, including contamination of soil and water resources through the use of persistent synthetic chemicals,” reads the lawsuit.

item.title: RenRe seeing strong third-party investor interest, but opts not to deploy Upsilon at mid-year: CEO O’Donnell
item.description: According to Kevin O’Donnell, CEO of RenaissanceRe, the reinsurer’s third-party capital and insurance-linked securities management unit, RenaissanceRe Capital Partners, is experiencing more capital interest in its collateralized vehicles than it can accommodate within its structures. However, speaking during the firm’s Q2 2026 earnings call this week, Bob Qutub, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of RenRe, explained that the reinsurer opted to not deploy its collateralized reinsurance and retrocession investment fund vehicle Upsilon at the mid-year renewals. Instead, the reinsurer chose to renew the business on wholly-owned balance sheets, which as Qutub explained, “should serve to limit the impact of the top line decrease on the bottom line of the vehicle.” Adding further context to this, O’Donnell explained that Upsilon was “relatively small anyway,” and alluded that this was a strategic decision that the company made for this year.

item.title: Allianz to acquire HSBC Life Singapore
item.description: Global insurer Allianz Group (Allianz), through its wholly owned subsidiary Allianz Asia Holding Pte Ltd, has agreed to acquire composite insurer HSBC Life Singapore Pte Ltd (HSBC Life Singapore) from HSBC Holdings plc (HSBC Group), subject to regulatory approval. HSBC Life Singapore has a strong presence in the country’s life and health insurance market. Allianz and HSBC Singapore will also enter into an exclusive 15-year distribution agreement.

item.description: Stock as president of Carolina Casualty, effective immediately. He initially joined Carolina Casualty, a Berkley company, in early 2025 as divisional president, where he led the transformation of the claims and risk management departments, in addition to several other functional areas. We are pleased that he has assumed the role of president at Carolina Casualty to lead our team in this dynamic market.” Operating nationwide, Carolina Casualty is a specialist in primary commercial insurance products and services for the transportation industry.

item.title: Kinsale’s net income jumps 31% to $175.9m in Q2’26
item.description: Kinsale said the increase in underwriting income was largely due to growth in net earned premiums and more favourable development of loss reserves from prior accident years, partially offset by lower ceding commissions as a result of increased retention on the company’s reinsurance treaties. Net investment income increased by 19.9% to $55.7 million from $46.5 million, driven by growth in Kinsale’s investment portfolio, largely resulting from the investment of strong operating cash flows. has reported a net income of $175.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, up 31% from $134.1 million in the same period a year prior.

item.title: Texas Panhandle Shaken by Strongest Earthquake to Hit the Region
item.description: A 5.0 magnitude earthquake rocked the Texas Panhandle early Thursday morning, one of the strongest recorded in Texas. Effects from the earthquake were felt throughout the rural region and as far as southern Oklahoma and New Mexico. Harrel said Thursday’s earthquake was stronger than what they typically see in the region.

item.title: People Moves: Shepherd Insurance Names Kleymeyer as President of Employee Benefits
item.description: Shepherd Insurance announced that Matt Kleymeyer has joined the firm as the President of Employee Benefits, further strengthening the organization’s commitment to delivering innovative employee benefits solutions and exceptional client service. As President of Employee Benefits, Kleymeyer will partner closely with Employee Benefits leadership team members Steve Gregory, Shannon Russell, and Susie Brancheau to help drive the continued growth and evolution of Shepherd Insurance’s benefits practice. Prior to joining Shepherd, Kleymeyer served as Area Executive Vice President and Indiana Market Leader at Gallagher, following the successful growth and sale of an employee benefits agency he co-founded.

item.title: Smart Glasses Transform Insurance Claims, Inspections
item.description: Smart glasses are standardizing insurance inspections through real-time documentation and AI-guided workflows that improve transparency and reduce claim processing delays. As AI capabilities continue to mature, AI smart glasses can also assist by identifying missing documentation, recognizing objects or damage patterns, and helping ensure that inspections meet established company guidelines before they are submitted. While some claims will always require an experienced adjuster to visit a site in person, smart glasses make it increasingly practical to conduct guided remote assessments for a wide range of property, vehicle, and equipment claims.

item.title: From System of Record to System of Action: AI in the AMS
item.description: That is the system-of-record-to-system-of-action shift: clean data captured at the point of entry is what lets the AMS act on the work, not just store a record of it. LLMs excel at this because the work is generative and the input – prior emails, account history, policy notes – already exists in the system. It also lives in a separate tab, disconnected from the system where the policy, the client, and the money actually live.

item.title: Adam Riese to acquire Neodigital’s insurance portfolio
item.description: Adam Riese , the digital insurance brand of Württembergische Versicherung, is taking over Neodigital Versicherung’s entire property, liability and accident insurance portfolio. Under a separate service agreement, Adam Riese will use Neodigital’s technology to manage both its existing policies and the acquired portfolio. item.title: Autonomous marks T&Cs as the new reinsurance battleground following mid-year rate declines
item.description: Referring to broker Guy Carpenter’s property catastrophe rate-on-line index which was down 16% at mid-year, accelerating down from -12% at the January 1 renewal, analysts at Autonomous noted that its refreshed analysis of contracts shows stable attachment points in absolute terms, although not keeping pace with inflation or cedent growth. A new report from Autonomous suggests that reinsurers are broadly keen to defend against any further loosening of terms and conditions (T&Cs), amid industry debate over the robustness of the response, leading the firm to note that T&C’s are now the new battleground. In this year’s renewal rounds, the reinsurers have suggested that T&Cs have held “broadly” stable, or words to the effect, while brokers have highlighted some forms of weakening,” Autonomous explained.

item.title: ILS, cat bonds & parametrics can help re/insurers innovate to expand nat cat coverage: Fitch
item.description: A new report from Fitch Ratings has suggested that insurance-linked securities (ILS), catastrophe bonds, and parametric insurance solutions can help re/insurers innovate in order to balance the conflicting goals of expanding access to affordable natural catastrophe cover, without impairing underwriting principles. Fitch also emphasises how the catastrophe bond market has continued to expand throughout the years, and how more re/insurers and sovereigns across the globe are turning to the capital markets to expand their nat cat protection. “Several jurisdictions have created regulatory frameworks for ILS to facilitate the issuance of cat bonds as an additional risk-transfer option for insurers.

item.title: LexisNexis Risk Solutions reports shifting trends in US home insurance claims
item.description: LexisNexis Risk Solutions, a provider of data, analytics and technology services for the insurance, financial services, healthcare and public sectors, has published its 2026 US Home Trends Report, outlining the latest developments in the US home insurance market. “US home insurers continue to face increasing pressure and uncertainty as they contend with a ‘perfect storm’ of rising severity, rising inflation-driven replacement costs and a reshaping of loss patterns in the face of shifting climate-driven catastrophes,” commented George Hosfield, Vice President and General Manager, Home Insurance, LexisNexis Risk Solutions. According to LexisNexis Risk Solutions, overall claims severity reached its highest recorded level in 2025, rising by 25.9% compared with the previous year and by 93.2% since 2019.

item.title: The Hartford sees strong Q2’26 results with 31% net income growth
item.description: US-based insurer The Hartford has announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026, reporting an increase in net income, to $1.3 billion, and 3% growth in Property & Casualty (P&C) written premiums compared to the same period last year. For Q2 2025, The Hartford’s net income increased 31% from the $990 million reported for the second quarter of 2025, driven by 5% growth in P&C earned premium and 5% fully insured ongoing premium growth in Employee Benefits. Also contributing to the results were a 3% increase in Property & Casualty (P&C) written premiums driven by Business Insurance premium growth, with the latest also seeing its combined ratio increase to 91.4 and an improved underlying combined ratio of 89.3.

item.title: World Bank Estimates Quakes Cost Venezuela $20 Billion in Damage
item.description: The twin earthquakes that hit Venezuela last month may have caused $19.6 billion in physical damage to buildings and infrastructure, or about 18% of gross domestic product , according to a preliminary assessment by the World Bank. The World Bank’s figure stands well below United Nations estimates of physical damage to housing and infrastructure of around $37 billion. “The bank will continue to be a technical partner, and we are undergoing assessments on how to support the government, including financing, to see ways in which we can crowd in private investment effectively.” A five-year reconstruction period would be possible if Venezuela mobilizes $9.8 billion in additional financing to support the fiscal response, and $9.6 billion in private investment, according to the report.

item.title: US Strikes Iran From South to North After Trump Threats Over Red Sea Shipping
item.description: missiles struck targets across Iran, reaching as far as its Caspian coast, on Friday after President Donald Trump vowed “major military punishment” for Tehran and its Houthi allies in Yemen for extending the Middle East war to a second major shipping chokepoint, the mouth of the Red Sea. The Iranian army said Trump’s threats only strengthened its resolve. Trump wrote on social media he would hold Iran accountable for any further attacks by the fighters, “and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves.” He told Axios he was considering re-launching major combat operations in Iran and was close to a decision.

item.title: US and Allies Say Russian Hackers Stole Emails Without Social Engineering
item.description: The United States and more than a dozen allied nations said on Thursday that Russian hackers stole emails from users of the Zimbra email program without having to fool them into opening an attachment or clicking a link. “No social engineering required,” Proofpoint said in a blog post outlining the hacking campaign. In April, Reuters reported Russian hackers had broken into scores of email accounts belonging to prosecutors and investigators across Ukraine.

item.title: Sompo to acquire Fator Seguradora
item.description: Sompo has agreed to acquire Brazilian commercial insurer Fator Seguradora . Sompo and Fator will continue operating independently until the deal closes. Founded in 2008, Fator specializes in commercial property, surety and financial lines, serving businesses in sectors including construction, energy, infrastructure and oil and gas.

item.title: Árachas Group acquires Allison White Insurance
item.description: Arachas Group , a Keystone platform partner, has acquired Allison White Insurance, an independent agency based in Little Falls, Minnesota. Allison White Insurance will maintain its local presence while gaining access to Árachas and Keystone’s resources and expertise. Founded in 2018 by Allison White, the agency serves individuals approaching Medicare eligibility, retirees and small businesses across central Minnesota.

item.title: New York Life adds indemnity option to Asset Flex
item.description: New York Life has added an indemnity benefit option to Asset Flex, its hybrid product combining long-term care coverage with universal life insurance. Asset Flex is available in most states through New York Life financial professionals and registered investment advisors. Customers can now choose between reimbursement coverage, which pays qualified care expenses up to a monthly limit, and an indemnity option that provides a monthly cash benefit once the policyholder qualifies for a claim, regardless of the actual expenses incurred.

item.title: Hybrids Boom as EVs Fall Out of Favor Even in California
item.description: Hybrids accounted for almost one in every four automobiles registered in California in the second quarter, according to newly released data from the California New Car Dealers Association. Hybrids, meanwhile, have benefited as the war in Iran has pushed gas prices higher. The national average was $4.02 for a gallon of gas as of Tuesday, while California’s is $5.52, according to AAA.

item.description: New Jersey’s high court has ruled that Allstate Insurance has a right to a jury trial for its fraud and conspiracy claims brought against more than 30 medical providers under the state’s Insurance Fraud Prevention Act (IFPA) and the Anti-Racketeering Act (RICO).
